claim: Current uncaging methods are limited by the random distribution of caged molecules within cells.
source: Current uncaging methods are limited by the random distribution of caged molecules within cells.
evidence: This is a statement made in the abstract describing a limitation of existing methods.

claim: A mitochondria-specific photoactivation method has been developed.
source: We have developed a mitochondria-specific photoactivation method, which permitted us to release free sphingosine inside mitochondria and thereafter monitor local sphingosine metabolism by lipidomics.
evidence: The abstract describes the development of this method as a primary finding of the study.

claim: Sphingosine was quickly phosphorylated into sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) driven by sphingosine kinases.
source: Our results indicate that sphingosine was quickly phosphorylated into sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) driven by sphingosine kinases.
evidence: This is stated as a result in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Mitochondria-specific uncaged sphingosine demonstrated distinct metabolic patterns compared to globally-released sphingosine.
source: In time-course studies, the mitochondria-specific uncaged sphingosine demonstrated distinct metabolic patterns compared to globally-released sphingosine, and did not induce calcium spikes.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by time-course experimental data.

claim: Mitochondria-specific uncaged sphingosine did not induce calcium spikes.
source: In time-course studies, the mitochondria-specific uncaged sphingosine demonstrated distinct metabolic patterns compared to globally-released sphingosine, and did not induce calcium spikes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by calcium mobilization experiments.

claim: Sphingolipid metabolism and signaling are highly dependent on the subcellular location.
source: Our data provide direct evidence that sphingolipid metabolism and signaling are highly dependent on the subcellular location and opens up new possibilities to study the effects of lipid localization on signaling and metabolic fate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Sphingolipids are one of the major lipid species in cellular membranes of all eukaryotic cells.
source: Sphingolipids are one of the major lipid species in cellular membranes of all eukaryotic cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge in the introduction.

claim: At least four sphingolipid metabolites (sphingosine, ceramide, sphingosine 1-phosphate, and ceramide 1-phosphate) are signaling messengers that regulate fundamental cellular processes.
source: Apart from maintaining structural properties of membranes, at least four sphingolipid metabolites, sphingosine, ceramide, sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) and ceramide 1-phosphate (C1P), are also signaling messengers that regulate fundamental cellular processes (Aguilera-Romero et al., 2014; Hannun and Obeid, 2008; Maceyka and Spiegel, 2014; Atilla-Gokcumen et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Aberrant sphingolipid levels are linked to a broad range of diseases, including cancers, diabetes, inflammation and neurodegeneration.
source: Due to their essential roles, aberrant sphingolipid levels are linked to a broad range of diseases, including cancers, diabetes, inflammation and neurodegeneration (Maceyka and Spiegel, 2014; Platt, 2014; Guri et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Sphingolipid messengers could serve distinct functions depending on their subcellular localization.
source: Interestingly, sphingolipid messengers could serve distinct functions depending on their subcellular localization, but this is currently difficult to address (Hannun and Obeid, 2008).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation, indicating it is a hypothesis or observation from prior work.

claim: Extracellular S1P activates receptors on the cell surface.
source: For example, extracellular S1P activates receptors on the cell surface (Lee et al., 1998; Van Brocklyn et al., 1998; Liu et al., 2000), while S1P generated inside the nucleus has been proposed to regulate histone acetylation through direct interactions with the histone deacetylases (HDAC) (Hait et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: S1P generated inside the nucleus has been proposed to regulate histone acetylation through direct interactions with the histone deacetylases (HDAC).
source: For example, extracellular S1P activates receptors on the cell surface (Lee et al., 1998; Van Brocklyn et al., 1998; Liu et al., 2000), while S1P generated inside the nucleus has been proposed to regulate histone acetylation through direct interactions with the histone deacetylases (HDAC) (Hait et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature and is described as a proposal.

claim: Several protein domains have been suggested to bind to S1P, which might affect the recruitment of many PH domains.
source: Furthermore, several protein domains have been suggested to bind to S1P, which might affect the recruitment of many PH domains (Vonkova et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and is described as a suggestion.

claim: There is no direct evidence to demonstrate that cellular localization is an important regulator of the metabolism and functions of sphingolipids.
source: Although cellular localization is likely to be an important regulator of the metabolism and functions of sphingolipids, there is no direct evidence to demonstrate this.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge prior to the current study.

claim: Photoactivation ('uncaging') has become a common way to quickly increase the lipid supply.
source: Alternatively, photoactivation ('uncaging') has become a common way to quickly increase the lipid supply.
evidence: This is a statement about established methods in the field.

claim: Photoactivation requires the chemical protection of the lipid head group using a photo-labile moiety, which blocks the lipid bioactivities.
source: This method requires the chemical protection of the lipid head group using a photo-labile moiety, which blocks the lipid bioactivities.
evidence: This is a description of how photoactivation methods work.

claim: A strong light flash can remove the protecting group within milli-seconds to seconds, releasing the bioactive lipids with high temporal resolution.
source: Once inside cells, a strong light flash can easily remove the protecting group within milli-seconds to seconds, and thereby release the bioactive lipids with high temporal resolution (Höglinger et al., 2014; Klán et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Caged lipids, including sphingosine, S1P, fatty acids, and phosphatidylinositol phosphates (PIPs) have been successfully applied in lipid signaling studies.
source: To date, a number of caged lipids, including sphingosine (Höglinger et al., 2015; Höglinger et al., 2017), S1P (Qiao et al., 1998), fatty acids (Nadler et al., 2015), and phosphatidylinositol phosphates (PIPs) (Subramanian et al., 2010) have been successfully applied in lipid signaling studies.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Coumarin and nitrophenyl derivatives are widely used as caging groups to mask bioactive small molecules.
source: To perform the photoactivation experiments, coumarin and nitrophenyl derivatives are widely used as caging groups to mask the bioactive small molecules (Klán et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Caged molecules are usually distributed in the cell randomly.
source: Nevertheless, the caged molecules are usually distributed in the cell randomly.
evidence: This is a statement about a limitation of existing caging methods.

claim: Selective uncaging is only achieved through sophisticated fluorescence microscopy that is able to produce a highly focused laser beam in a defined area at the subcellular level.
source: Selective uncaging is only achieved through sophisticated fluorescence microscopy that is able to produce a highly focused laser beam in a defined area at the subcellular level.
evidence: This is a statement about the methods required for selective uncaging.

claim: It is very difficult to exclusively activate the compartment of interest due to the diffraction limit of light.
source: This method has disadvantages, though, because it is very difficult to exclusively activate the compartment of interest due to the diffraction limit of light.
evidence: This is a statement about a limitation of selective uncaging methods.

claim: The 'selective uncaging' strategy is limited to single-cell analysis, and hence is not suitable for biochemical assays that are needed to study metabolism.
source: More importantly, this 'selective uncaging' strategy is limited to single-cell analysis, and hence is not suitable for biochemical assays that are needed to study metabolism.
evidence: This is a statement about a limitation of selective uncaging methods.

claim: A new mitochondria-targeted photoactivation method enabled the rapid release of sphingosine inside the mitochondria in living cells.
source: Here, we report a new mitochondria-targeted photoactivation method, which enabled the rapid release of sphingosine inside the mitochondria in living cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the introduction.

claim: After photo-release, free sphingosine was rapidly phosphorylated into S1P, driven by sphingosine kinases.
source: We observed that after photo-release, free sphingosine was rapidly phosphorylated into S1P, driven by sphingosine kinases.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the introduction.

claim: Inhibition of sphingosine kinases largely suppressed the S1P generation.
source: Inhibition of sphingosine kinases largely suppressed the S1P generation.
evidence: This is a finding from the study stated in the introduction.

claim: Sphingosine was quickly lost indicating that these signaling sphingolipids are rapidly metabolized even when targeted to mitochondria.
source: In both cases, sphingosine was quickly lost indicating that these signaling sphingolipids are rapidly metabolized even when targeted to mitochondria.
evidence: This is a finding from the study stated in the introduction.

claim: Sphingosine metabolism was highly dependent on its subcellular localization.
source: Using stable isotope-labeled caged sphingosine precursors, we investigated the conversion of sphingosine into ceramides and sphingomyelins after uncaging, and found that sphingosine metabolism was highly dependent on its subcellular localization.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the introduction.

claim: Mitochondria released sphingosine was used to continuously produce ceramides.
source: Mitochondria released sphingosine was used to continuously produce ceramides, whereas globally released sphingosine was more rapidly metabolized through sphingolipid metabolic network.
evidence: This is a finding from the study stated in the introduction.

claim: Globally released sphingosine was more rapidly metabolized through sphingolipid metabolic network.
source: Mitochondria released sphingosine was used to continuously produce ceramides, whereas globally released sphingosine was more rapidly metabolized through sphingolipid metabolic network.
evidence: This is a finding from the study stated in the introduction.

claim: The Mito-So failed to trigger calcium mobilization, demonstrating the importance of lipid localization in signal transduction.
source: In contrast to the globally distributed Sph-Cou, the Mito-So failed to trigger calcium mobilization, demonstrating the importance of lipid localization in signal transduction.
evidence: This is a finding from the study stated in the introduction.

claim: 7-amino coumarin was modified by introducing a carboxylic linker and a methyl group.
source: In order to determine the subcellular localization of caged molecules in cells, we chose to modify the 7-amino coumarin (1) by introducing a carboxylic linker and a methyl group.
evidence: This describes a synthetic step in the methods.

claim: SeO2-mediated hydroxylation at the benzylic position afforded compound (3).
source: SeO2-mediated hydroxylation at the benzylic position afforded (3).
evidence: This describes a synthetic step in the methods.

claim: TFA deprotection of the t-Bu ester allowed facile conjugation to a triphenylphosphonium (TPP) group via an amide bond to afford TPP-Cou-OH (4).
source: TFA deprotection of the t-Bu ester allowed facile conjugation to a triphenylphosphonium (TPP) group via an amide bond to afford TPP-Cou-OH (4).
evidence: This describes a synthetic step in the methods.

claim: The lipophilic TPP cation is the best known mitochondria tag that facilitates accumulation of functional groups into mitochondrial matrix.
source: Introduced by Murphy and co-workers (Murphy, 1997; Murphy, 2008), the lipophilic TPP cation is the best known mitochondria tag that facilitates accumulation of functional groups into mitochondrial matrix.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Caged sphingosine (Mito-So) and sphinganine (Mito-Sa) were synthesized using the TPP-labeled coumarin alcohol (TPP-Cou-OH).
source: Using the TPP-labeled coumarin alcohol (TPP-Cou-OH), we synthesized caged sphingosine (Mito-So) and sphinganine (Mito-Sa) following standard protocols (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the synthesis of the caged compounds and references Figure 1.

claim: Most of the sphingosine was cleaved from the Mito-So after one minute of UV exposure.
source: Most of the sphingosine was cleaved from the Mito-So after one minute, judging from the coumarin absorbance (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a result from uncaging experiments, supported by data in Figure 2B.

claim: Both Mito-So and Mito-Sa were completely cleaved after two minutes compared to Sph-Cou.
source: Compared to Sph-Cou, both Mito-So and Mito-Sa were completely cleaved after two minutes (Figure 2C), indicating the TPP-Cou-OH is an effective photolabile molecule.
evidence: This is a result from uncaging experiments, supported by data in Figure 2C.

claim: TPP-Cou-OH is an effective photolabile molecule.
source: Compared to Sph-Cou, both Mito-So and Mito-Sa were completely cleaved after two minutes (Figure 2C), indicating the TPP-Cou-OH is an effective photolabile molecule.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the uncaging efficiency data.

claim: The caged probes are fluorescent dyes that emit in the blue region.
source: On the other hand, our measurement also indicated that the caged probes are fluorescent dyes that emit in the blue region (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from spectroscopic measurements, supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The pattern of Mito-So fluorescence completely overlaps with MitoTracker.
source: The pattern of Mito-So fluorescence completely overlaps with MitoTracker (Figure 2D,E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), demonstrating Mito-So and Mito-Sa are predominantly targeted to mitochondria.
evidence: This is a result from fluorescence microscopy experiments, supported by data in Figures 2D, 2E, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mito-So and Mito-Sa are predominantly targeted to mitochondria.
source: The pattern of Mito-So fluorescence completely overlaps with MitoTracker (Figure 2D,E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), demonstrating Mito-So and Mito-Sa are predominantly targeted to mitochondria.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the colocalization data.

claim: The accumulation of Mito-So in mitochondria relies on the integrity of mitochondrial membrane potential.
source: Like other TPP-containing mitochondria targeting molecules (Murphy, 2008), this accumulation relies on the integrity of mitochondrial membrane potential.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and is consistent with known properties of TPP-containing molecules.

claim: When the mitochondrial membrane potential is disrupted by CCCP, the mitochondria staining of Mito-So was not seen and the probe was randomly distributed throughout the cell.
source: When the potential is disrupted by CCCP, the mitochondria staining of Mito-So was not seen (Figure 2F) and the probe was randomly distributed throughout the cell.
evidence: This is a result from experiments using CCCP, supported by data in Figure 2F.

claim: Both sphingosine and S1P levels were dramatically elevated compared to the controls after uncaging Mito-So.
source: The results show that both sphingosine and S1P levels were dramatically elevated compared to the controls (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is a result from lipidomics experiments, supported by data in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: Sphinganine and sphinganine 1-phosphate (Sa-1P) were also increased after uncaging of Mito-Sa.
source: Similarly, sphinganine and sphinganine 1-phosphate (Sa-1P) were also increased after uncaging of Mito-Sa (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is a result from lipidomics experiments, supported by data in Figures 3C and 3D.

claim: The sphinganine level after Mito-Sa uncaging is higher compared to the sphingosine level after uncaging Mito-So.
source: Interestingly, the sphinganine level after Mito-Sa uncaging is higher compared to the sphingosine level after uncaging Mito-So; the opposite effects were observed in the phosphorylated form.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing the lipidomics data.

claim: Sphingosine is better recognized as a substrate for phosphorylation than sphinganine.
source: Since we treated the cells with equal amount of the probes, the results might reflect the fact that sphingosine is better recognized as a substrate for phosphorylation and/or that that Mito-Sa is more efficiently accumulated inside the cells.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data comparing sphingosine and sphinganine phosphorylation.

claim: Mito-Sa is more efficiently accumulated inside the cells than Mito-So.
source: Since we treated the cells with equal amount of the probes, the results might reflect the fact that sphingosine is better recognized as a substrate for phosphorylation and/or that that Mito-Sa is more efficiently accumulated inside the cells.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data comparing sphingosine and sphinganine levels.

claim: Mito-So and Mito-Sa were sufficiently stable and were not cleaved by enzymatic activities such as esterases during the experiments without photoactivation.
source: As a control, we examined the stability of Mito-So and Mito-Sa without photoactivation in the intracellular environments, and found no significant effects on sphingoid bases, showing that the Mito-caged lipids were sufficiently stable and were not cleaved by enzymatic activities such as esterases during the experiments.
evidence: This is a result from control experiments.

claim: The sphinganine level remained stable after Mito-So uncaging.
source: In addition, although sphingosine and sphinganine are structurally very similar, the sphinganine level remained stable after Mito-So uncaging (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), and vice versa (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is a result from lipidomics experiments, supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The sphingosine level remained stable after Mito-Sa uncaging.
source: In addition, although sphingosine and sphinganine are structurally very similar, the sphinganine level remained stable after Mito-So uncaging (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), and vice versa (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is a result from lipidomics experiments, supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Both sphingosine and S1P were slightly reduced after UV exposure without any caged probe.
source: Although both lipids were slightly reduced after UV exposure (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), the reduction is rather minimal and is in the opposite direction compared to the effects of uncaging, showing that the effect of UV illumination is insignificant under these conditions.
evidence: This is a result from control experiments, supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The effect of UV illumination on sphingosine and S1P levels is insignificant under these conditions.
source: Although both lipids were slightly reduced after UV exposure (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), the reduction is rather minimal and is in the opposite direction compared to the effects of uncaging, showing that the effect of UV illumination is insignificant under these conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the control experiments.

claim: The major lipid species and ceramides were not affected after Mito-So and Mito-Sa uncaging.
source: Likewise, the major lipid species and ceramides were not affected after Mito-So and Mito-Sa uncaging (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: This is a result from lipidomics experiments, supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D,E.

claim: These photochemical probes, upon illumination, effectively released sphingoid bases with high spatiotemporal resolution.
source: Taken together, our results demonstrate that these photochemical probes, upon illumination, effectively released sphingoid bases with high spatiotemporal resolution.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The increased amount of S1P was due to phosphorylation of sphingosine by sphingosine kinases.
source: Since sphingosine and S1P are interconvertible molecules, we assumed that the increased amount of S1P was due to phosphorylation of sphingosine by sphingosine kinases.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated by the authors.

claim: There are two isoforms of sphingosine kinases in mammalian cells, sphingosine kinase 1 (SphK1) and sphingosine kinase 2 (SphK2), both of which are capable of phosphorylating sphingosine into S1P.
source: There are two isoforms of sphingosine kinases in mammalian cells, sphingosine kinase 1 (SphK1) and sphingosine kinase 2 (SphK2), both of which are capable of phosphorylating sphingosine into S1P (Maceyka et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: SphK double knock-out (dKO) cells failed to raise the S1P level after uncaging, in contrast to the control cells in which significantly elevated S1P was detected.
source: As expected, SphK double knock-out (dKO) cells failed to raise the S1P level after uncaging, in contrast to the control cells in which significantly elevated S1P was detected (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a result from experiments using knockout cells, supported by data in Figure 4B.

claim: Removing sphingosine kinases did not disrupt mitochondria morphology or membrane potential.
source: After showing that removing sphingosine kinases did not disrupt mitochondria morphology or membrane potential (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), we carried out uncaging experiments using Mito-So in the cell lines and measured their sphingolipid levels.
evidence: This is a result from control experiments, supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: SKI-II treated cells generated less S1P, and increased the level of sphingosine after uncaging.
source: Consistent with the results in the knockout cells, SKI-II treated cells generated less S1P, and increased the level of sphingosine (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is a result from experiments using the inhibitor SKI-II, supported by data in Figures 4C and 4D.

claim: SKI-II did not fully block S1P synthesis, which might be due to the fact that the SKI-II and sphingosine are competitive substrates for the kinases.
source: The SKI-II did not fully block S1P synthesis, which might be due to the fact that the SKI-II and sphingosine are competitive substrates for the kinases (Lim et al., 2012; French et al., 2003), and/or the access of SKI-II to the mitochondria might be limited.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data, supported by citations.

claim: The access of SKI-II to the mitochondria might be limited.
source: The SKI-II did not fully block S1P synthesis, which might be due to the fact that the SKI-II and sphingosine are competitive substrates for the kinases (Lim et al., 2012; French et al., 2003), and/or the access of SKI-II to the mitochondria might be limited.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: The rapid S1P accumulation after uncaging was catalyzed by sphingosine kinases.
source: Taken together, our results clearly show that the rapid S1P accumulation after uncaging was catalyzed by sphingosine kinases.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Sphingosine kinases were not able to use the caged lipids as substrates in vivo even though the hydroxyl group was available.
source: These results show that sphingosine kinases were not able to use the caged lipids as substrates in vivo even though the hydroxyl group was available, which further supports our conclusion that S1P accumulation is due to sphingosine kinase activity on the uncaged sphingoid bases.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experiments where lipids were extracted before uncaging.

claim: After UV irradiation of purified mitochondria with Mito-So, an elevated sphingosine level was detected.
source: Consistent with live-cell experiments, after UV irradiation, we detected an elevated sphingosine level (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a result from experiments using purified mitochondria, supported by data in Figure 5A.

claim: A significant increase in S1P was observed in purified mitochondria after uncaging Mito-So, which was suppressed by the addition of the SKI-II inhibitor.
source: Importantly, we also observed a significant increase in S1P, which was suppressed by the addition of the SKI-II inhibitor (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a result from experiments using purified mitochondria, supported by data in Figure 5B.

claim: The phosphorylation of sphingosine into S1P was less efficient in purified mitochondria compared with live-cell experiments.
source: Compared with Figure 3B, the phosphorylation of sphingosine into S1P was less efficient in purified mitochondria, which might have been due to the different experimental settings and the intrinsic activity of purified mitochondria compared to mitochondria in vivo.
evidence: This is an observation comparing data from different experiments.

claim: Extra-mitochondrial S1P was not detected in the assay using purified mitochondria, probably due to its relatively high solubility in aqueous buffers.
source: We therefore conclude that the S1P found in our assay was indeed inside mitochondria as extra-mitochondrial S1P was not detected in our assay, probably due to its relatively high solubility in aqueous buffers.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from control experiments where exogenous S1P was added.

claim: At least part of the released sphingosine was phosphorylated inside mitochondria.
source: Collectively, our data demonstrate that, upon illumination, free sphingosine was quickly released from Mito-So in the mitochondria and was partially and rapidly converted into S1P by SphKs. The rapid phosphorylation, together with our results using purified mitochondria, provide convincing evidence that at least part of the released sphingosine was phosphorylated inside mitochondria.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Sphingosine kinases are partially localized to mitochondria.
source: This is consistent with reports finding that sphingosine kinases are partially localized to mitochondria (Lim et al., 2012; Strub et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The decay of sphingosine (t1/2 = 2.63 min) generated from Mito-So is much faster than the one from Sph-Cou (t1/2 = 4.21 min).
source: Notably, the decay of sphingosine (t1/2 = 2.63 min, Figure 6C) generated from Mito-So is much faster than the one from Sph-Cou (t1/2 = 4.21 min, Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a result from time-course experiments, supported by data in Figures 6C and 6E.

claim: Sphingosine released from Sph-Cou did not drop to the basal level even after 20 min, suggesting that part of the globally released sphingosine was stored inside cells.
source: Also, unlike the Mito-So, sphingosine released from Sph-Cou did not drop to the basal level even after 20 min, suggesting that part of the globally released sphingosine was stored inside cells, which prevented further metabolism during the time course.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the time-course data.

claim: In both cases (Mito-So and Sph-Cou), the released sphingosine was quickly metabolized without affecting the amounts of other major lipid species.
source: Not surprisingly, in both cases, the released sphingosine was quickly metabolized without affecting the amounts of other major lipid species (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from time-course experiments, supported by data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Sphingosine levels still declined over time in SphK dKO cells after uncaging Mito-So, but the half-life was significantly longer than in wild type cells (t1/2 = 4.2 min).
source: Even though major lipid species were not affected (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), sphingosine levels still declined over time, but the half-life was significantly longer than in wild type cells (t1/2 = 4.2 min, Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a result from time-course experiments in knockout cells, supported by data in Figure 6D.

claim: Sphingosine turnover in SphK dKO cells was the result of its conversion into ceramide by ceramide synthases.
source: Since S1P formation and sphingoid base turnover were blocked, the most logical explanation is that sphingosine turnover was the result of its conversion into ceramide by ceramide synthases, but this did not affect the total ceramide pool since steady state levels of ceramide in HeLa cells are much higher than sphingosine or S1P levels.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data from knockout cells.

claim: Both d7-labeled C16 and C24 ceramides were detected immediately after uncaging of d7-Mito-So, demonstrating a rapid conversion to ceramide.
source: As shown in Figure 7 (left), we detected both d7-labeled ceramides immediately after uncaging of d7-Mito-So, demonstrating a rapid conversion to ceramide.
evidence: This is a result from experiments using isotope-labeled probes, supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: The amount of newly formed ceramides steadily increased even after 20 min following d7-Mito-So uncaging.
source: The amount of newly formed ceramides steadily increased even after 20 min.
evidence: This is a result from time-course experiments using isotope-labeled probes.

claim: Globally localized d7-Sph-Cou generated a distinct metabolic pattern compared to d7-Mito-So.
source: Interestingly, globally localized d7-Sph-Cou generated a distinct metabolic pattern (Figure 7, middle).
evidence: This is a result from experiments using isotope-labeled probes, supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: Fewer ceramides were formed at 0 min after d7-Sph-Cou uncaging and both ceramides reached their maximum after 5 to 10 min and dropped significantly after 20 min.
source: Fewer ceramides were formed at 0 min and both ceramides reached their maximum after 5 to 10 min and dropped significantly after 20 min, suggesting that the ceramides were quickly consumed to synthesize other sphingolipids.
evidence: This is a result from time-course experiments using isotope-labeled probes.

claim: The ceramides formed after d7-Sph-Cou uncaging were quickly consumed to synthesize other sphingolipids.
source: Fewer ceramides were formed at 0 min and both ceramides reached their maximum after 5 to 10 min and dropped significantly after 20 min, suggesting that the ceramides were quickly consumed to synthesize other sphingolipids.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the time-course data.

claim: Directly added d7-sphingosine showed continuous accumulation and sharp increase of ceramides over time, indicating that sphingosine entered from outside was efficiently metabolized by cells.
source: As for directly added d7-sphingosine, we observed continuous accumulation and sharp increase of ceramides over time, indicating that sphingosine entered from outside was efficiently metabolized by cells.
evidence: This is a result from experiments using directly added isotope-labeled sphingosine.

claim: The signals of d7 C16 sphingomyelin increased over time in all cases.
source: We also analyzed the signals of d7 C16 sphingomyelin and observed that, while the signals were increased over time in all cases, the signals generated after global release of d7 Sph-Cou uncaging was close to reaching a plateau, unlike the externally added and mitochondrial released d7 Sph that were still in an early phase.
evidence: This is a result from experiments using isotope-labeled probes.

claim: The signals of d7 C16 sphingomyelin generated after global release of d7 Sph-Cou uncaging was close to reaching a plateau, unlike the externally added and mitochondrial released d7 Sph that were still in an early phase.
source: We also analyzed the signals of d7 C16 sphingomyelin and observed that, while the signals were increased over time in all cases, the signals generated after global release of d7 Sph-Cou uncaging was close to reaching a plateau, unlike the externally added and mitochondrial released d7 Sph that were still in an early phase.
evidence: This is a result from experiments using isotope-labeled probes.

claim: Only part of the ceramide population was readily converted to sphingomyelin.
source: The lower sphingomyelin signals, compared to ceramides, suggests that only part of the ceramide population was readily converted to sphingomyelin.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data comparing ceramide and sphingomyelin signals.

claim: Subcellular localization is important for sphingolipid metabolism.
source: Our data provide direct evidence that subcellular localization is important for sphingolipid metabolism.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The rapid turnover of sphingosine suggests that lipid metabolism studies require techniques with high temporal resolution.
source: The rapid turnover also suggests that lipid metabolism studies require techniques with high temporal resolution.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Global uncaging of sphingosine quickly induced calcium release as previously reported.
source: As shown here, global uncaging of sphingosine quickly induced calcium release as previously reported, whereas mitochondria specific uncaging failed to trigger any calcium mobilization in the saame time frame ( Figure 8, Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from calcium mobilization experiments, supported by data in Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mitochondria specific uncaging failed to trigger any calcium mobilization in the same time frame as global uncaging.
source: As shown here, global uncaging of sphingosine quickly induced calcium release as previously reported, whereas mitochondria specific uncaging failed to trigger any calcium mobilization in the saame time frame ( Figure 8, Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from calcium mobilization experiments, supported by data in Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The amount of sphingosine found after uncaging was approximately two times higher for Mito-So than for Sph-Cou.
source: The amount of sphingosine found after uncaging was approximately two times higher for Mito-So than for Sph-Cou (Figure 8—figure supplement 2), showing that differences in the amount of probe taken up by the cells is not the explanation for the different physiological consequences.
evidence: This is a result from quantification experiments, supported by data in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Differences in the amount of probe taken up by the cells is not the explanation for the different physiological consequences between Mito-So and Sph-Cou.
source: The amount of sphingosine found after uncaging was approximately two times higher for Mito-So than for Sph-Cou (Figure 8—figure supplement 2), showing that differences in the amount of probe taken up by the cells is not the explanation for the different physiological consequences.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the quantification data.

claim: Intracellular sphingoid base compartmentalization can be a deciding factor in the regulation of intracellular signal transduction.
source: Our data thus provide direct evidence that the intracellular sphingoid base compartmentalization can be a deciding factor in the regulation of intracellular signal transduction.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the calcium mobilization experiments.

claim: Glycerophospholipids and sphingolipids are unequally distributed among the subcellular structures of the cell.
source: It is clear that glycerophospholipids and sphingolipids are unequally distributed among the subcellular structures of the cell, however, the transport of lipids is very rapid, with phosphatidylethanolamine being transported from its site of the synthesis to the plasma membrane in less than a couple of minutes (Sleight and Pagano, 1983).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The transport of lipids is very rapid, with phosphatidylethanolamine being transported from its site of the synthesis to the plasma membrane in less than a couple of minutes.
source: It is clear that glycerophospholipids and sphingolipids are unequally distributed among the subcellular structures of the cell, however, the transport of lipids is very rapid, with phosphatidylethanolamine being transported from its site of the synthesis to the plasma membrane in less than a couple of minutes (Sleight and Pagano, 1983).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: A highly efficient photo-cleavable probe (TPP-Cou-OH) has been developed that can be easily installed on the amino group of free sphingoid bases.
source: To address this, we have developed a highly efficient photo-cleavable probe (TPP-Cou-OH) that was easily installed on the amino group of free sphingoid bases, and which can be potentially applied to mask other functional groups, allowing the caging of a wide variety of lipids and other bioactive molecules.
evidence: This is a description of the probe developed in the study.

claim: TPP-Cou-OH can be potentially applied to mask other functional groups, allowing the caging of a wide variety of lipids and other bioactive molecules.
source: To address this, we have developed a highly efficient photo-cleavable probe (TPP-Cou-OH) that was easily installed on the amino group of free sphingoid bases, and which can be potentially applied to mask other functional groups, allowing the caging of a wide variety of lipids and other bioactive molecules.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential applications of the probe.

claim: The caged probes accumulated in mitochondria, into which the entry is tightly regulated.
source: Carrying a hydrophobic and positively charged triphenylphosphonium (TPP) cation, the caged probes accumulated in mitochondria, into which the entry is tightly regulated.
evidence: This is a description of the properties of the caged probes.

claim: The caged probes can be used for single-cell microscopic analysis as well as biochemical experiments to follow metabolism.
source: In contrast, our caged probes can be used for single-cell microscopic analysis as well as biochemical experiments to follow metabolism.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities of the caged probes developed in the study.

claim: Combining mass-spectrometry (MS)-based lipidomic approaches with the caged probes produced a robust system that enabled monitoring of local sphingosine metabolism in living cells.
source: Combining this approach with our caged probes produced a robust system that enabled us to monitor the local sphingosine metabolism in living cells.
evidence: This is a description of the combined methodology used in the study.

claim: Uncaging sphingosine in purified mitochondria also generated a significant amount of S1P, providing strong evidence that mito-released sphingosine was phosphorylated inside mitochondria.
source: Importantly, uncaging sphingosine in purified mitochondria also generated a significant amount of S1P, providing strong evidence that mito-released sphingosine was phosphorylated inside mitochondria, consistent with previous studies that claimed SPHKs are detected in the mitochondria (Strub et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experiments using purified mitochondria.

claim: Ceramide is pro-apoptotic, whereas S1P promotes cell growth and proliferation.
source: It has been known that ceramide is pro-apoptotic, whereas S1P promotes cell growth and proliferation.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge.

claim: The functions of sphingosine, which can be metabolized into ceramide and S1P, are not well understood.
source: But the functions of sphingosine, which can be metabolized into ceramide and S1P, are not well understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Mitochondria is a major hub of energy supply and has been highly associated with apoptosis.
source: Since mitochondria is major a hub of energy supply and has been highly associated with apoptosis, it is interesting to investigate the metabolism of mitochondrial sphingosine, and to compare this with the metabolism globally distributed sphingosine.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge.

claim: Ceramides are much more abundant lipids than sphingoid bases in cells.
source: Since ceramides are much more abundant lipids than sphingoid bases in cells ((Simanshu et al., 2013; Shaner et al., 2009; Canals et al., 2010), Figure 3—figure supplement 1), we prepared stable isotope labelled caged sphingosine so that the newly produced ceramides can be distinguished from the endogenous pool of ceramides by mass spectrometry.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ceramide synthases (CerS), which catalyze the conversion of sphingosine into ceramide, are mainly located in endoplasmic reticulum (ER).
source: Since ceramide synthases (CerS), which catalyze the conversion of sphingosine into ceramide, are mainly located in endoplasmic reticulum (ER), the lack of substrate accessibility to CerS may prevent immediate ceramide formation from liberated sphingosine in mitochondria.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge.

claim: The lack of substrate accessibility to CerS may prevent immediate ceramide formation from liberated sphingosine in mitochondria.
source: Since ceramide synthases (CerS), which catalyze the conversion of sphingosine into ceramide, are mainly located in endoplasmic reticulum (ER), the lack of substrate accessibility to CerS may prevent immediate ceramide formation from liberated sphingosine in mitochondria.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: The slow sphingosine exit from mitochondria resulted in the continuous increase of ceramides.
source: It is likely that the slow sphingosine exit from mitochondria resulted in the continuous increase of ceramides.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: Globally uncaged sphingosine is easily accessible to CerS, which could explain the rapid ceramide production and degradation.
source: On the other hand, globally uncaged sphingosine is easily accessible to CerS, which could explain the rapid ceramide production and degradation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: No preferential synthesis of ceramides with specific acyl chain length dependent upon the localized source of sphingosine was detected.
source: We did not detect a preferential synthesis of ceramides with specific acyl chain length dependent upon the localized source of sphingosine.
evidence: This is a result from the experiments using isotope-labeled probes.

claim: Less ceramides were detected from globally released sphingosine compared to mitochondrial sphingosine.
source: Interestingly, we detected less ceramides from globally released sphingosine.
evidence: This is a result from the experiments using isotope-labeled probes.

claim: Mitochondrial sphingosine is more efficiently, but less rapidly transferred to the ER, the site of ceramide production.
source: One possibility is that mitochondrial sphingosine is more efficiently, but less rapidly transferred to the ER, (Figure 8—figure supplement 2) the site of ceramide production.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data, supported by data in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Sphingosine produced in the mitochondria can enter the sphingolipid biosynthetic pathway.
source: It is clearly shown from our data that sphingosine produced in the mitochondria can enter the sphingolipid biosynthetic pathway, demonstrating that there is a pathway to transfer sphingosine from the mitochondrial matrix to the ER.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: There is a pathway to transfer sphingosine from the mitochondrial matrix to the ER.
source: It is clearly shown from our data that sphingosine produced in the mitochondria can enter the sphingolipid biosynthetic pathway, demonstrating that there is a pathway to transfer sphingosine from the mitochondrial matrix to the ER.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Mitochondrial sphingosine does not freely and rapidly diffuse in the cells because it would have produced a release of calcium.
source: This clearly shows that the mitochondrial sphingosine does not freely and rapidly diffuse in the cells because it would have produced a release of calcium.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the calcium mobilization experiments.

claim: The exit from mitochondria might be too slow to be seen in the time course of calcium mobilization experiments.
source: Why does it not produce a calcium release? Two factors might influence this. One, it could be that the exit from mitochondria is too slow to be seen in our time course.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the calcium mobilization data.

claim: Mitochondrial sphingosine could be transported preferentially to the ER.
source: Second, it could be that the mitochondrial sphingosine is transported preferentially to the ER. This would be consistent with the increased efficiency of ceramide synthesis from mitochondrial sphingosine compared to global sphingosine.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: Externally added sphingosine is also targeted preferentially to the ER as it behaves similarly to mitochondrial sphingosine.
source: It is possible that externally added sphingosine is also targeted preferentially to the ER as it behaves similarly to mitochondrial sphingosine.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: Site-specific photochemical probes will become valuable tools in lipid signaling and metabolism studies.
source: We envision that site-specific photochemical probes will become valuable tools in lipid signaling and metabolism studies.
evidence: This is a forward-looking statement about the potential impact of the work.
